records.name: Resolve Philly
records.summary: A local news group for Philadelphia neighborhoods. It sends free text updates in English and Spanish, runs a Germantown news site, and publishes G-Town Beat, a series of community briefings on topics like property rights.
records.what_you_do: Text EQUAL INFO to 215-910-4040 for free updates, subscribe to the Germantown newsletter, share a story or resource for the Equally Informed newsletter, ask about becoming an Info Hub Captain, or come to a G-Town Beat briefing.

schedule.text: Text updates and newsletters go out on an ongoing basis. Briefings are posted on the Germantown news site as they are scheduled.

cost.text: The text service is free. The site does not state a cost for the newsletters or briefings.

first_step.how: Text EQUAL INFO to 215-910-4040 to start getting free updates in English or Spanish. To attend a briefing, check the Germantown Info Hub for the next one.
first_step.basis: Anyone can join the free text service or a newsletter in one step, and the site says how. It does not say how a first briefing works or whether a reservation is needed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The one briefing we read about ran from 6 to 8:30 pm in person at The Braid Mill in Germantown, with speakers from city offices and a legal services group on property and estate topics. The site does not say whether it cost money or needed a reservation.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the group holds townhalls. The townhall items on the site are updates on restoring the Germantown Town Hall building, not public meetings, so that claim was dropped. Text frequency is described as weekly in one post and monthly in others, so the schedule gives no fixed rhythm. The G-Town Beat briefing article (event on September 24, 2026, article dated October 6, 2026) names Germantown United CDC as the host and gives no cost or registration details. The site's contact email is hidden behind email protection and was not recorded. Not recorded: the festival listing (says Oct. 3, no year on the page), the job posting, and the donation page. Germantown United CDC is in leads_only.

records.name: Roll With Respect
records.summary: A youth development group for Philadelphia young people ages 6 to 24. It offers tutoring and educational support, mentoring, and leadership workshops on creative expression, money habits, mental health, and civic life.
records.what_you_do: Email the group to ask about tutoring or a youth program. The site lists four leadership workshop topics: creative expression, money habits, mental health and consumer choices, and civic leadership.

first_step.how: Email rollwithrespect@gmail.com and ask how a young person joins tutoring or a youth program. The site does not describe an enrollment step.
first_step.basis: The site names tutoring and youth programs and gives an email address, but it does not say how to join, where programs meet, or when they run, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes the work in general terms but does not say how a session runs, how long it lasts, who leads it, or what it costs. Ask those questions when you email.

records.notes: The site has no dates, schedule, program locations, costs, or enrollment steps, so the status rests on a working site alone. The about page mentions 2019 only in connection with the founder's personal loss, not the group's start, so no founding year is recorded. The founder named on the site is Brandon Miller. Conflict resolution, which tier 1 listed, does not appear on the site, so it was dropped. The Instagram link on the site has no URL and was not recorded.

records.name: Scene-N-Action Productions
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs dance and theater classes for children and adults, plus performance companies. Classes include ballet, jazz, tap, hip-hop, creative theater, a toddler movement class, and adult dance.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a class through the Classes/Register page. The site also names several performance companies, listed on the Creative Directors page with the classes each director leads.

schedule.text: Class terms run from fall 2026 into 2027. Days and times are not on the public pages we could read.

cost.text: Prices are in a linked fall 2026 price list, and the site says pricing may change in January 2027. Monthly fees are paid through a separate online payment page.

first_step.how: Open the Classes/Register page on snapcompany.org and use the fall 2026 registration link, or call (267) 420-2810 with questions before you sign up.
first_step.basis: The site lists beginner tap and a toddler movement class and gives a clear registration link, so beginners are welcome to sign up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists classes for toddlers, beginners, and adults, plus ballet, jazz, hip-hop, and tap groups. It does not say how long a class runs, what a single class costs, or whether a first class can be tried before paying.

records.notes: Class days, times, and per-class prices are only in a linked fall 2026 price list (PDF) and a registration form, neither of which we could open. The Programs page names no classes and shows only a flyer image, so it was not used as a source. The tier 1 email snap2times@gmail.com is replaced by info@snapcompany.org from the group's contact page. The tier 1 label 501(c)(3) does not appear on the site, so the record says nonprofit only. The contact page has no office hours, parking, or transit notes.

records.name: Tennessee Program
records.summary: A nonprofit that works with young people on skills, character, and mentoring. Its programs include auto technician training, photography, fitness, a lifestyle course, and a music and engineering class. It has also run book bag drives and food giveaways for people experiencing homelessness.
records.what_you_do: Contact the group to ask about joining a youth program or helping on a service day. Past service days include book bag drives and food and supply giveaways.

first_step.how: Call (267) 670-5098 or email info@tennesseeprogram.com, and ask about the program you want. The contact page says to contact the group to sign up.
first_step.basis: The site asks people to contact the group to sign up but does not describe enrollment steps, ages, or start dates, so the way in is unclear. The music class says no prior experience is needed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The auto class has students do hands-on work on vehicles of many makes and models. The basics the site lists include changing tires and oil and working on brakes. The music class covers recording, mixing, and production with studio equipment. The site does not say how long a session runs, what it costs, or where most classes meet.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the group's site is the August 2023 book bag drive, more than 24 months old, so status is dormant. The verdict is left as publish for a human to decide, since nothing newer was found on the site. One web search for the group and its contact name found nothing newer. The home page summary mentioned cleanups and gardening, but the community service page lists no specific activities, so they are not recorded. No program page gives days, times, ages, costs, or start dates. The auto class Sign up button has no link destination. The contact name comes from tier 1 directory data and does not appear on the pages read. Not fetched: the Support, Donate, and Our Team pages.

records.name: Voices of Burnout
records.summary: A nonprofit online community about preventing burnout. It shares blog posts, videos, and quotes, and runs a Facebook group where people connect and ease the isolation that comes with burnout.
records.what_you_do: Read the blog and share the posts, join the Facebook community group to talk with others, send a comment through the contact form, or sign the petition on change.org about laws to reduce burnout.

cost.text: No charge is listed for reading, following, or joining online.

first_step.how: Join the Facebook community group, or add your email on voicesofburnout.org to get updates.
first_step.basis: The site lists several open ways to follow along, including an email signup, a contact form, and a Facebook group.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe live meetings or events. A first visit is mostly reading the blog posts about burnout. If you want to take part, you can leave a comment, send a message through the contact form, or join the Facebook group.

records.notes: The newest dated blog post is August 18, 2025, about 14 months old, so status is probably_active. The About page names Patricia Osborne Randolph as creator and president, with board members Julie Thomas and Christine Picard (board names not recorded). The calendar_feed is the post RSS link listed on the home page; it was not opened. The Engage link goes to the author's personal WordPress page and was not used. The Facebook group and the change.org petition were linked only and not read. The site gives no street address beyond 'Located in Philadelphia, PA'.

records.name: Water Tower Advisory Council
records.summary: A 501(c)(3) nonprofit that guides how the Water Tower Recreation Center is developed and used, working with Philadelphia Parks & Recreation and the local community. The center has gyms, courts, ball fields, a playground, and classrooms.
records.what_you_do: The main way to take part is to join the Advisory Council. The site says council meetings are open to the public and listed on its calendar, but the calendar showed no meetings when we checked. The center's programs page lists an after school program, pickleball, gymnastics, and a youth sport club, with details on linked pages.

schedule.text: Council meetings are open to the public. The site does not give a regular meeting day or time.

first_step.how: Use the Contact page at wtrec.org/contact to ask how to take part in the council, and ask when the next open meeting is, since the site does not list one.
first_step.basis: The site says council meetings are open to the public, but gives no meeting dates, times, or address, and the only step listed is the contact page, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe what a council meeting is like, how long it lasts, or where it is held. It names the council's officers and says the council works with the parks department and the community toward shared goals.

records.notes: No dated evidence on the site: the calendar and the Future Updates heading are empty, so status is probably_active on a working site alone. The programs page names four items: an after school program (details on a linked page), Chestnut Hill Youth Sport Club (a separate organization, in leads_only), pickleball (phone 215-685-9296 is listed on the page), and gymnastics (details on a linked page). The after school and gymnastics pages were not fetched because the six-fetch budget for this group was used. Board officers named on the About page are not recorded. The contact page lists social links only, with no email or phone.

records.name: Way Moore Justice Support
records.summary: A group that works with people who say they were wrongly convicted, along with their families and lawyers, through Pennsylvania's post-conviction process. It also runs talks, courses, and workshops on wrongful convictions and restorative justice.
records.what_you_do: Attend a talk, film discussion, or course the group takes part in. The site lists a wrongful convictions course with Mt. Airy Learning Tree on October 22, 2026, and past talks at a Rotary club and several universities.

schedule.text: Talks, courses, and workshops are announced on the site when they are scheduled. The site does not give a regular weekly or monthly time.

first_step.how: Open the Upcoming Workshops page on waymoorejustice.org and use the Register Here link for the October 22, 2026 wrongful convictions course. That link goes to the Mt. Airy Learning Tree registration page.
first_step.basis: The course page says anyone interested in civics, social justice, or the legal system can take it, and it gives a register link. One past talk was for members and guests, and the site does not say what the course costs.
first_step.what_to_expect: The course is listed at Essential Community Connections on Germantown Avenue, taught by Tricia Way and Yahya Moore. The site does not say how many sessions it runs, how long each one lasts, or what it costs.

records.notes: Last sign of life is the October 22, 2026 course listed on the Upcoming Workshops page, a future-dated listing. The newest past dated item is the August 2026 Rotary talk. The course price, length, and schedule are not stated. The contact name Patricia Way comes from tier 1 directory data; the site names Tricia Way as an instructor. Tier 1's winter and spring 2026 course is replaced by the October 2026 course. Course registration is handled by Mt. Airy Learning Tree, a partner, so that site was not opened and is in leads_only. The partners page names two foundation funders, in leads_only. Services and Our Team pages were not read.

leads_only.note: Named as the host of the September 2026 G-Town Beat briefing on the Resolve Philly site, not checked.

notes: All 7 groups in batch w23-026 were read and written. Fetches: 34 (six per group at most; batch cap 60). WebSearch: 1 of 1 used, on Tennessee Program to look for newer evidence; nothing newer was found. Tennessee Program is dormant by the 24 month rule (newest dated item August 2023) but is kept at verdict publish for a human decision. Several tier 1 claims were corrected and are explained in each record's notes: Resolve Philly townhalls, Scene-N-Action email and category, Tennessee service activities, Voices of Burnout cost wording, Way Moore course date.
